extracted.intended_audience: Prospective applicants to the ARPA‑E OPEN 2021 FOA (small businesses, companies, universities, national labs, research teams)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation/procedural rules for preparing and submitting concept papers and full applications to the ARPA‑E OPEN 2021 Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA), including eligibility, cost share, IP, budget, team composition, and review criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subrecipient and contractor determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Please see 2 CFR § 200.331 - Subrecipient and contractor determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the governing federal rule referenced for questions about restrictions on partnering/subcontracting, allowability of fee for small business subcontractors performing a commercial service, and determining whether a collaborator is a contractor or subrecipient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant eligibility (domestic entities / small businesses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must meet the criteria and eligibility concerns outlined in the FOA (Section III.A. ELIGIBLE APPLICANTS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small businesses CAN apply. For‑profit organizations and other entity definitions are in the FOA glossary; eligibility determinations depend on the submitted Project Team and must follow FOA rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign entity participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Refer to FOA Section III. Eligibility Information 3. Foreign Entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions about whether a foreign university or foreign partner may appear on a proposal as a subcontractor (and how much work/budget they may be assigned) are governed by the FOA's foreign entity rules; applicants should consult that FOA section.

rubrics_metrics.name: FFRDCs / DOE Labs participation limits
rubrics_metrics.description: FFRDCs/DOE Labs are eligible to apply for funding as the lead organization for a Project Team or as a member of a Project Team that includes institutions of higher education, companies, research foundations, or trade and industry research collaborations, but not as a Standalone Applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Section II.C (ARPA‑E Funding Agreements) for funding agreements and any additional requirements for proposals involving federal labs or FFRDCs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost sharing general requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The ARPA‑E eXCHANGE 'requires applicants to contribute at least 20% of the total project cost.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must follow the FOA's Cost Sharing section (Section B) and federal cost share standards (2 C.F.R. § 200.306). ARPA‑E will not pre‑assess applicants' cost share arrangements; prospective applicants must independently determine compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduced cost share and cost share grace period
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduced Cost Share Requirement and Cost Share Grace Period (see FOA Section III.B.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small businesses may be eligible for reduced cost share (e.g., 10%) or a grace period allowing 0% cost share during the first 12 months, per the FOA text. The eXCHANGE system allows applicants to expand or modify the Project Team after concept submission, so cost share partners need not always be locked in at submission (see related Qs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal rules on cost share accounting
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal standards for cost share may be found at 2 C.F.R. § 200.306.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should use federal cost share rules to determine what counts as cost share (cash vs in‑kind), timing, and allowability. ARPA‑E will not pre‑assess specific arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect cost rate / de minimis and cost share interplay
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions about whether reducing an applicant's negotiated indirect cost rate and counting the difference as cost share must be evaluated against FOA and federal rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ARPA‑E will not pre‑assess such arrangements; applicants must review the FOA and federal guidance to determine whether a lower indirect cost rate can be credited as cost share. The FOA also discusses the 10% de minimis indirect rate for entities without a negotiated rate—see FOA for basis ('10% of what').

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of submissions and scientific distinctness
rubrics_metrics.description: ARPA‑E is not limiting the number of submissions from Applicants. Applicants may submit more than one application to this FOA, provided that each application is scientifically distinct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A firm may submit multiple proposals under separate topic areas and potentially receive multiple awards if each application is scientifically distinct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award amounts, anticipated number of awards, and period of performance
rubrics_metrics.description: ARPA‑E expects to make approximately $100 million available and anticipates making approximately 30‑50 awards. Individual awards may vary between $250,000 and $10 million in Federal share. The period of performance for funding agreements may not exceed 36 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are planning expectations stated in the FOA (see Section II.A); ARPA‑E may at its discretion issue one, multiple, or no awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical Category / Subcategory selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may select a single Technical Subcategory or multiple Technical Subcategories for their proposed technology, as appropriate. The Applicant may select multiple Technical Subcategories from the same Technical Category or different Technical Categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a technology spans multiple categories/subcategories, applicants may submit one concept paper covering multiple subcategories as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit review / evaluation criteria (concept paper and full application)
rubrics_metrics.description: Refer to FOA Section V.A.1 for Concept Paper evaluation criteria, including V.A.1(2) (team composition/qualifications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project team composition and qualifications are assessed as an element of merit review. Evaluation criteria for Full Applications are expected to be published (June 2021) and generally include similar criteria. Applicants should consult FOA V.A.1 and related sections for detailed scoring guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer expectations about assumed knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Refer to FOA Section V.B.2 for information about ARPA‑E reviewers (e.g., whether to assume reviewer familiarity with a given technical background).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing concept summaries, applicants should follow FOA guidance about what background reviewers are expected to have and whether to include fundamental descriptions of widely known technical concepts.

rubrics_metrics.name: ARPA‑E will not pre‑assess fit or proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: ARPA‑E will not pre‑assess an applicant’s proposal. Prospective applicants must review the technical requirements of the FOA and independently determine whether their proposed concept warrants a submission and which subtopic to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should not expect program managers to pre‑screen or advise on the appropriateness of a specific concept for the FOA; instead use FOA text, FAQs, and webinars to self‑assess fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concept paper and full application budget requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For the concept paper, applicants provide estimated totals under the funds and costs tab. Applicants must complete all budget information in section D. Content and Form of Full Applications 3. THIRD COMPONENT: BUDGET JUSTIFICATION WORKBOOK/SF‑424A of the FOA for full applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget details beyond concept paper estimates are required for full applications; follow FOA instructions for the budget justification workbook and SF‑424A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable costs — prototype, hardware, equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: Prototype development and hardware costs are allowable expenses under this FOA. Equipment definitions and purchase of new equipment are in FOA section G. Funding Restrictions 7. Purchase of New Equipment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult FOA section G for the definition of capital equipment (dollar thresholds) and any restrictions on purchasing equipment with award funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance audit requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: See Section J. Compliance Audit Requirement of the FOA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should review what funding conditions trigger a mandatory audit and whether audit costs may be budgeted into the project or charged to G&A; the FOA provides the compliance audit rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual Property management and title to inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: ARPA‑E requires every Project Team to negotiate and establish an Intellectual Property Management Plan for the management and disposition of intellectual property arising from the project. See section B. Administrative and National Policy Requirements 7. Intellectual Property and Data Management Plans of the FOA and Section VIII.A. Title to Subject Inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FOA discusses whether applicants may retain title to subject inventions and addresses government rights (e.g., Government Use License, March‑In Rights, Rights in Technical Data). Applicants must follow the FOA IP template and related guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class patent waiver practice
rubrics_metrics.description: ARPA‑E typically issues class patent waivers, but not definitively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants with partners who require a patent waiver should note ARPA‑E's typical practice but cannot rely on a guaranteed waiver unless specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team composition preferences and PI/co‑PI rules
rubrics_metrics.description: ARPA‑E has stated no preference for composition of project teams (.gov, .edu, .com). Co‑PIs are allowed. The PI must meet all eligibility requirements for applicants as stated in the FOA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project team composition and qualifications are evaluated during merit review; applicants may list co‑PIs in concept/full submissions per FOA templates and instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modifications after concept paper (team and budget)
rubrics_metrics.description: The ARPA‑E eXCHANGE system will allow applicants to expand or otherwise modify the Project Team. Team members and funding amounts are not permanently locked in at concept paper submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If selected to submit a full proposal, applicants may change team composition and budget details in the eXCHANGE system in accordance with FOA rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation of individuals on multiple teams
rubrics_metrics.description: Yes, you are allowed to participate in multiple teams. Participating on multiple teams as a Co‑PI and leading one proposal as PI is permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be mindful of potential conflicts of interest during review; ARPA‑E allows multiple participations but reviewers/administrators will manage COI per FOA processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on coupling with other Federal reimbursement programs
rubrics_metrics.description: OPEN 2021 cannot be coupled with other Federal reimbursement programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an applicant has received federal reimbursement from another program (e.g., prizes with payments), they should ensure that applying to OPEN 2021 would not constitute impermissible coupling under FOA rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: No SBIR set‑aside within OPEN 2021
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no SBIR portion pertaining to the OPEN 2021 solicitation. Note: Small businesses may apply to the OPEN 2021 FOA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants looking for SBIR‑specific mechanisms should note OPEN 2021 is a separate ARPA‑E FOA and not an SBIR competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions and follow‑on funding not guaranteed
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional funds and extensions are possible, but not guaranteed at this time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan project timelines within the FOA's maximum period of performance; do not assume follow‑on ARPA‑E funding or extensions unless announced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to find further FOA details (sections referenced repeatedly)
rubrics_metrics.description: Many detailed answers and requirements point the applicant to specific FOA sections: Section I.D (Technical Categories), II.A (Award Information), III (Eligibility), IV (Application and Submission), V (Evaluation and Selection), VIII (Other Information — Title to Subject Inventions), G (Funding Restrictions), J (Compliance Audit), and B (Cost Sharing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should consult the specified FOA sections for authoritative rules and templates (e.g., IP Management Plan template), and use the ARPA‑E eXCHANGE system and FOA text as primary references. ARPA‑E will not pre‑assess compliance or fit beyond what is published.
